newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: South Australia to abolish interstate cheque duty.
newsitem.headline: South Australia to abolish interstate cheque duty.

text.p: The South Australian government is to abolish the payment of stamp duty on interstate cheques banked in the state, Premier John Olsen said on Monday.
Olsen said in a statement the decision, to take effect on January 1, 1998, affected more than six million transactions each year which were currently subject to a ten cent duty.
"Having to pay stamp duty on interstate cheques is a major irritant to small business," he said.
"It amounts to a penalty on South Australian companies that are trading interstate and because it is a fixed charge, it impacts more on small businesses than larger businesses," he said.
